knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for Go 1.21+. Loaded automatically when agents work on .go files, go.mod, or go.sum. Covers project structure, error handling, concurrency, interfaces, testing standards, and tooling for microservices, APIs, and CLIs.

core-principles.principle: Prefer simple, readable code over clever solutions. Obvious is better than elegant.
Use goroutines and channels for concurrent operations. Always pass context.Context for cancellation and timeouts.
Explicit error handling — no exceptions. Always check errors; never silently ignore them.
Use interfaces and struct embedding instead of inheritance hierarchies.
Go's stdlib is rich. Minimize external dependencies; add only when the value is clear.

guardrail.rule: Always check returned errors. Never discard with _ unless justified by a comment explaining why.
Never panic in library or service code. Panic only for truly unrecoverable programmer errors (e.g., impossible state in init). Return errors instead.
Wrap errors with context using fmt.Errorf and %w so callers can inspect the chain with errors.Is / errors.As.
guardrail.bad: return nil, err // loses call-site context return nil, errors.New("error occurred") // vague
guardrail.good: return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch user %s: %w", id, err)

guardrail.rule: Pass context.Context as the first argument to every function that does I/O, network calls, or database queries. Always set a timeout on outgoing HTTP requests.
Run gofmt (or goimports) and go vet before every commit. Code that does not pass go vet must not be merged.
guardrail.good: go fmt ./... go vet ./... golangci-lint run

guardrail.rule: Package names must be lowercase with no underscores. Exported identifiers use PascalCase; unexported use camelCase.
guardrail.bad: package user_service // underscore in package name type user_repo struct {} // underscore in type

guardrail.rule: Accept interfaces, return concrete types (structs). Define interfaces at the point of use, not at the point of implementation. Keep interfaces small (1-3 methods ideal).
Use sync.WaitGroup for goroutine coordination. Close channels only from the sender side. Use select with a default case to avoid blocking.
guardrail.bad: close(ch) // called from receiver — data race / double-close risk

guardrail.rule: No global mutable variables. Use dependency injection via function parameters or struct fields.
Use parameterized queries for all database operations. Never concatenate user input into SQL strings.
guardrail.bad: query := "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '" + id + "'" db.QueryRow(query)
guardrail.good: db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", id)

guardrail.rule: Run go mod tidy before committing. Pin major versions in go.mod. Use Go 1.21+ with modules — no GOPATH-era patterns.
guardrail.bad: // go.mod missing go directive or with unpinned versions

guardrail.rule: Use custom domain error types for domain-level errors so callers can distinguish them with errors.As.
guardrail.bad: return fmt.Errorf("not found") // caller cannot type-check this

directory.purpose: Main applications — one subdirectory per executable
Entry point; wire dependencies and start server
Private application code — not importable by other modules
Business logic, domain types, and domain errors
Data access — database queries and storage
Public reusable libraries — only for code genuinely useful to external callers
Module definition; pin major versions here
Dependency checksums — always commit this file

pattern.name: Table-Driven Tests
pattern.context: Any function with multiple input/output cases
pattern.description: Define test cases in a slice of anonymous structs; iterate with t.Run for isolated subtests. Use t.Helper() in helper functions. This is the idiomatic Go testing pattern.

pattern.name: Dependency Injection via Constructor
pattern.description: Pass all dependencies through a constructor function. This makes the type testable (inject mocks) and prevents hidden global state.

pattern.name: HTTP Handler with Context Propagation
pattern.description: Extract context from the request; pass it to all downstream calls. Log at appropriate levels; return structured error responses.

pattern.name: Goroutine Fan-Out with WaitGroup
pattern.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch N goroutines and wait for all to finish. Collect errors through a buffered channel.

testing.pattern: go test -race ./... // always run in CI; catches data races at test time
